request: is that a permissions issue? Why would the btrfs report no usable inode count in the mount? Research

references.finding: Btrfs creates inodes dynamically without fixed inode tables; metadata space and utilization bound creation.

references.author: David Sterba
references.finding: The maintainer states that Inode/IFree numbers are intentionally zero and objects to invented estimates.

references.author: Qu Wenruo
references.finding: Dynamic metadata/tree overhead makes simple free-inode estimates unreliable.
The generic code zero-initializes the statistics buffer and returns a security-hook error before filesystem statistics collection.
The upstream Btrfs implementation populates block statistics without assigning f_files or f_ffree.
Undefined filesystem-specific fields are zero; path-prefix search denial returns EACCES.
The execute bit means search permission for directories; capabilities can separately bypass discretionary access checks.
